mentions.text:
Honestly I think just picking up on the mood among institutional investors can give you a real edge.

For example I attended an investment conference when I was in New York this year and Samsung Life Insurance was named there as an undervalued stock.

Just a few days later foreign institutions bought Samsung Life in size.

If you had been at that conference you could have made a decent return.

Want another example?

I'm in TMT BreakOut, a Substack Slack with a lot of institutional investors. Just from the chat there I can get hints about where institutions are focused right now.

A few weeks ago someone posted "Why is everyone suddenly going long NVDA?" Now NVDA is at an ATH.

I think there's a lot of value in retail being able to pick up on this kind of sentiment.
